data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Engineering Cameras (Hazcams and Navcams)
record.description: There are two types of Engineering Cameras on the Mars Exploration Rover, the Hazard avoidance cameras (Hazcams) and the Navigation cameras (Navcams). There are four Hazcams, two mounted on the lower front of the rover and two on the lower rear. They are black and white visible light cameras with a field of view of about 120 x 120 degrees. The cameras view the terrain up to three meters in front of and behind the rover to detect any obstacles in the path of the rover. The camera output is interpreted by software which directs the rover to avoid any perceived hazards. The two Navcams are mounted on the rover mast as a stereo pair. They take visible light panoramic images with a 45 x 45 degree field of view to assist in navigation of the rover, and also assist the hazard avoidance imaging by giving a higher perspective of the ground.
